title: Redesign quickstart entryflow illustration and step microcopy for new onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Refresh the Quickstart landing entry experience (hero, process diagram, and step microcopy) to reduce cognitive load for first-time API users and highlight the three deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Deliverables: 1) Hero illustration set (svg + png fallbacks) with three contextual states: Developer (fast integration), Ops (security/Private), and Platform (Dedicated capacity). 2) Condensed three-step diagram with animated micro-interactions for web (Lottie or CSS animation) and a static SVG fallback. 3) Updated step-by-step microcopy and CTA variants for free-tier vs. enterprise. 4) Annotated screenshot pack for marketing and docs (desktop and mobile). Constraints: Keep assets performant (svg-first), accessible (text alternatives and color contrast), and easily localizable. Coordinate with Engineering for screenshot capture hooks (staging tokens) and with PM for messaging alignment.
acceptance_criteria: Hero variants implemented in staging and validated in Chrome/Firefox/Safari desktop and mobile
Three-step diagram reduces average time-to-first-request in usability test (pilot with 10 users) vs baseline by >= 15%
Microcopy approved by PM and Legal (no claim language), and localized in en, fr, de for release
All SVGs have <10KB baseline and include title/desc for screen readers
Design handoff includes redlines, asset export presets, and implementation notes in Confluence
comments: 2026-02-19 — Kickoff: aligned with PM (Jon Rivera) on core metrics: time-to-first-request, conversions from signup to API key, and accessibility score target >= 90.

2026-03-11 — Engineering implementation note: CSS prefers svg-sprite with inline <svg> for animation hooks; recommend delivering both inline-ready SVGs and optimized external files. Front-end to review handoff on 2026-03-13.
2026-03-12 — Usability pilot scheduled for 2026-03-16 with 12 participants (mix of PMs, engineers, and platform leads); success criteria reiterated in Acceptance Criteria.
